dedupe_keys.name: weham forest development and timber supply model waldentwicklungs und holzaufkommensmodellierung

description: WEHAM is the German model for forest development and timber supply. Starting from the forest state measured in the Bundeswaldinventur 2022 and from assumptions about growth and future forest management, it estimates how the forest and the potential raw wood supply will develop, here for 2023 to 2062. The data, assumptions and control conditions together with the results form a scenario; the federal government and the states jointly defined the WEHAM 2022 base scenario, which reflects current silvicultural practice and expectations. The page explains that when economic conditions, management or forest structure change, for example through large windthrow, bark beetle outbreaks or climate change, the input data must be updated and the model adjusted, producing a new scenario. The results are free to read online; no licence is stated and the model software itself is not offered on the page. Caveats: the page says WEHAM can hardly model factors important for biodiversity, such as deadwood decay or habitat trees, and the pages are in German. Coverage is Germany. It supports climate adaptation and capacity planning for forest green infrastructure; the related record is the Bundeswaldinventur results database.
